review_comments.body:
**[Medium] Merge per-call overrides before expanding parameters**

With `temperature=0` on the model, `invoke(..., temperature=0.5)` now raises `TypeError` because `_generate` expands both `_identifying_params` and `kwargs` as separate keyword arguments. The same regression affects the other newly retained zero values and all four generation/streaming paths. Replace the separate expansions with `**{**self._identifying_params, **kwargs}` in `_generate`, `_agenerate`, `_stream`, and `_astream` so per-call values take precedence.
@pcbeingused333 Could you please check this comment? Thanks!

comments.body:
Thanks @herohua, and thanks to Copilot for catching this: with `temperature=0` now retained on the model, `invoke(..., temperature=0.5)` expanded the same key twice and raised `TypeError`. Pushed a follow-up commit that merges the model defaults and the call kwargs into one mapping (`**{**self._identifying_params, **kwargs}`) in `_generate`, `_agenerate`, `_stream` and `_astream`, so the per-call value wins. Added a test covering all four paths (red before the change, green after).

Disclosure: this change was prepared with an AI coding assistant.

Please fix the test typing in `libs/azure-ai/tests/unit_tests/test_chat_models.py` before merging. At line 612, `messages` is inferred as `list[HumanMessage]`, while `_generate`, `_agenerate`, `_stream`, and `_astream` expect `list[BaseMessage]`. This causes four mypy errors and leaves the required CI check failing ([log](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-azure/actions/runs/41758336198/job/126339742915?pr=1269)).

Add `BaseMessage` to the existing `langchain_core.messages` import and annotate the list:

```python
messages: list[BaseMessage] = [HumanMessage(content="hi")]
```

Then rerun lint and confirm CI passes.
